blocks.text: Polyatomic ions are ions composed of more than one type of atom. Their formal charge is the net charge on them, calculated from the number of electrons in their valence shells after the bonds have formed. With the exception of the ammonium ion NH4+, these ions mostly carry a negative charge, for example carbonate CO3 2-, sulfate SO4 2- and nitrate NO3 - (printed as NO3 3-). In some polyatomic ions the central atom violates the octet rule by expanding its electron density into higher orbitals; these are said to have expanded octets. Prominent examples are SO4 2-, ClO4 - and PO4 3-.

From the Lewis structure of SO4 2-, the number of electrons around the central sulfur atom is 2 x (double bond electrons) + 2 x (single bond electrons) = 2(4) + 2(2) = 12. So sulfur has 12 electrons in its valence shell and exceeds the octet by four. The expansion is caused by the involvement of the d orbital in bonding, which can accommodate the extra electrons. The configuration of a native S(0) atom shows two unpaired electrons in the 3p orbitals; the presence of the 3d orbital allows this to extend to four unpaired electrons by the transfer of one electron from the 3p pair. This explains not only the variable oxidation states of sulfur but also its ability to accept extra electrons in its d orbital.

In the same way, the valence electrons around the central iodine atom of the tri-iodide ion I3- are 2 x (single bond electrons) + 2 x (lone pairs) = 2(2) + 2(3) = 10. The central iodine has 10 electrons in its valence shell, and the octet expands by two.

blocks.prompt: Can the elements of period 2 have an expanded octet? Predict and explain the expanded octets in ClO3- and PO4 3-.
blocks.explanation: No: period 2 atoms (C, N, O, F) have only 2s and 2p orbitals, no d orbitals, so they cannot hold more than eight valence electrons. Chlorine and phosphorus are in period 3 and have empty 3d orbitals. In ClO3- the chlorine makes two double bonds and one single bond and keeps a lone pair, 2(4) + 2(1) + 2(1) = 12 electrons; in PO4 3- the phosphorus makes one double bond and three single bonds, 2(2) + 2(3) = 10 electrons. Both exceed the octet by using 3d orbitals.

items: Polyatomic ions have more than one kind of atom; most are negative (NH4+ is the exception). A central atom of period 3 or beyond can expand its octet into d orbitals: S in SO4 2- has 12 valence electrons, I in I3- has 10.
